summary: Lemborexant is a dual orexin receptor antagonist (DORA) and Schedule IV controlled substance indicated for the treatment of insomnia characterized by difficulties with sleep onset and/or sleep maintenance in adults. It works by blocking the binding of the wake-promoting neuropeptides orexin-A and orexin-B to OX1 and OX2 receptors, thereby suppressing wakefulness. The recommended starting dose is 5 mg taken once nightly immediately before going to bed, with at least 7 hours remaining before the planned time of awakening; the dose may be increased to a maximum of 10 mg based on response and tolerability. Because it is habit forming and a CNS depressant, key risks include next-day somnolence and impaired driving, complex sleep behaviors (sleep-walking, sleep-driving), sleep paralysis, and worsening of depression/suicidal ideation. It should not be used in patients with narcolepsy.
indications: Treatment of insomnia, characterized by difficulties with sleep onset and/or sleep maintenance, in adults

dosage.d: 5 mg once per night immediately before bedtime; may increase to a maximum of 10 mg once nightly based on response
dosage.n: At least 7 hours before planned awakening

admin: Take immediately before going to bed, only when at least 7 hours can be devoted to sleep before the planned time of awakening
Take on an empty stomach; taking with or soon after food delays onset of effect
Do not increase the dose more often than every several days; do not exceed 10 mg
Avoid activities requiring full alertness (including driving) until the effects on the individual are known
Dispense as a controlled substance (Schedule IV); store securely to prevent diversion
moa: Lemborexant is a dual orexin receptor antagonist (DORA). The orexin (hypocretin) neuropeptide system - orexin-A and orexin-B acting at OX1 and OX2 receptors - promotes wakefulness and arousal. Lemborexant binds competitively to both OX1R and OX2R and blocks the binding of orexin neuropeptides, thereby suppressing the wake drive and facilitating the transition to and maintenance of sleep. Unlike GABAergic hypnotics, it modulates the sleep-wake switch rather than producing global CNS depression.

relative: Moderate hepatic impairment (limit to 5 mg); severe hepatic impairment (not recommended)
History of depression or suicidal ideation
History of substance abuse (habit-forming, Schedule IV)
Compromised respiratory function (e.g., severe OSA, severe COPD)
monitor: Complex sleep behaviors (sleep-walking, sleep-driving) and sleep paralysis
Worsening depression or emergence of suicidal thoughts
Signs of misuse, abuse, or dependence

preg: There are no adequate human data on lemborexant use in pregnancy to assess drug-associated risk. Animal studies showed developmental toxicity only at exposures well above the recommended human dose. Use during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk; a pregnancy exposure registry may be available.
lact: It is not known whether lemborexant is present in human milk or its effects on the breastfed infant or milk production. Because of the potential for sedation in the infant, weigh the developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding against the mother's clinical need and any potential adverse effects.
renal: No dosage adjustment is required for renal impairment. Lemborexant exposure is not meaningfully altered across renal-function categories.
hepatic: No adjustment is needed for mild hepatic impairment. In moderate hepatic impairment, limit the dose to a maximum of 5 mg once nightly because of increased exposure and prolonged half-life. Use is not recommended in severe hepatic impairment.

major: Strong CYP3A inhibitors (ketoconazole, clarithromycin, itraconazole) - avoid concomitant use (markedly increased lemborexant exposure)
Strong CYP3A inducers (rifampin, carbamazepine, St John's wort) - avoid; reduce efficacy
Other CNS depressants (opioids, benzodiazepines, alcohol) - additive sedation and respiratory depression
moderate: Moderate CYP3A inhibitors - avoid concomitant use
Weak CYP3A inhibitors - limit lemborexant to 5 mg
CYP3A substrates with narrow index - lemborexant may modestly affect exposure
minor: Drugs causing daytime drowsiness - additive next-day impairment
interactions.food: Taking with or shortly after food delays time to onset; take on an empty stomach. Avoid grapefruit (CYP3A inhibition).
interactions.alcohol: Avoid alcohol - additive CNS depression, impaired next-day function, and increased risk of complex sleep behaviors.
interactions.diagnostics: No specific laboratory interference established; consider drug-screen awareness given controlled-substance status.

serious: Complex sleep behaviors (sleep-walking, sleep-driving, performing activities while not fully awake)
CNS depression and next-day driving/psychomotor impairment
Cataplexy-like symptoms (mild leg weakness) and respiratory depression in compromised patients
emergency: Sleep-driving or other complex behavior leading to injury
Acute respiratory depression in vulnerable patients

monitoring: Assess for next-day somnolence and driving/psychomotor impairment
Ask about complex sleep behaviors and discontinue if any occur
Monitor mood and for new or worsening depression/suicidal thoughts
Reassess the need for continued treatment and watch for signs of misuse or dependence
Re-evaluate if insomnia persists beyond 7-10 days (may indicate underlying disorder)
counsel: Take it right before bed only when you can stay in bed at least 7 hours; do not take it if you must wake sooner
Take it on an empty stomach - a meal will delay how quickly it works
Do not drink alcohol or take other sedating medicines with it, and do not drive until you know how it affects you the next day
Stop and call your doctor if you do things in your sleep you do not remember (walking, driving, eating)
This medicine can be habit forming - take only as prescribed, do not increase the dose on your own, and tell your doctor about any mood changes or thoughts of self-harm
pk: Time to peak concentration approximately 1-3 hours; delayed by food
Effects span the sleep period; risk of next-day residual effects
Store at controlled room temperature (20-25 C); keep secured as a controlled substance
pearls: Schedule IV controlled substance - habit forming; prescribe and store securely and counsel on misuse/dependence
Dual orexin receptor antagonist suppresses wakefulness rather than causing global GABAergic sedation
Contraindicated in narcolepsy; can precipitate cataplexy-like or sleep-paralysis symptoms
Complex sleep behaviors (sleep-driving) can occur even at recommended doses and without alcohol - discontinue if they occur
Take on an empty stomach with at least 7 hours of intended sleep; avoid co-administration with strong/moderate CYP3A inhibitors and inducers
missed: Lemborexant is taken only at bedtime as needed for sleep. If a dose is missed, skip it and do not take it later in the night; take the next dose at the usual bedtime only if at least 7 hours of sleep time remain. Do not take two doses at once.
overdose: There is no specific antidote for lemborexant overdose. Overdose may cause exaggerated CNS depression with profound somnolence. Provide general supportive care, monitor cardiorespiratory status, and consider standard measures for CNS depressant overdose; dialysis is not expected to be useful given high protein binding. Contact a poison control center for current management guidance.
